opener: NORTHLINE BANK ALERT: Suspicious login detected on your account from device in TX. If this was NOT you, verify your identity immediately: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: Impersonate Northline Bank fraud alert. Cite a suspicious login from a specific but generic location (TX). Create fear of account compromise.
stages.scriptedFallback: For security, your online access has been temporarily locked. Verify your identity within 2 hours to restore access.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: They replied. Confirm their last 4 digits are on file (use ***1234 format). Ask them to verify by clicking the link to 'unlock' their account.
stages.scriptedFallback: We have an account ending in ***1234 flagged. Please verify via the secure link so we can unlock it immediately.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Escalate — there's a $1,200 transfer pending from their account to an unknown payee. It will process in 30 minutes unless they verify.
stages.scriptedFallback: ⚠️ A $1,200 transfer is pending to an unrecognized account. It processes in 30 minutes. Verify NOW to block it: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Ask them to log in through the link and enter their username, password, and the one-time code their bank will send.
stages.scriptedFallback: Log in at {{PRACTICE_LINK}} and enter the code Northline will text you. This confirms your identity and blocks the transfer.

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. Never enter your bank credentials or one-time codes from a text link.

hook.explanation: Account compromise fear triggers immediate action without thinking
Real bank alerts send you to the official app, not an SMS link
Scammers copy bank alert formats exactly, including capitalized sender names

engage.explanation: Generic last-4 confirmation (any 4 digits work) falsely validates legitimacy

escalate.explanation: '30 minutes to process' is a manufactured crisis designed to skip verification steps

ask.explanation: Asking for your one-time code through a text link gives scammers real-time access to your account
Real bank fraud teams NEVER ask for your OTP — that code is only for you
